docs.title: Agent Setup
docs.text: Shared agent configuration lives in .agents/.

docs.title: Claude Code
docs.text: $ make claude

docs.title: Other Agents
docs.text:
Symlink .agents/AGENTS.md and .agents/rules/ wherever your agent expects them.

If you use a different agent, consider contributing a make <agent> target to the Makefile so others can get started with one command.

docs.title: Build and Run
docs.text: This project utilizes CGO for low-level networking capabilities, requiring specific dependencies and build flags.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Go Version: Go 1.26 or higher is required.
  • C Compiler: A C compiler (GCC or Clang) must be available on your system.
  • Network Dependency: The project relies on the libpcap library for packet capture functionality. You must install the development headers for this library before building.

docs.title: Dependency Installation Examples
docs.text: Distribution Command Debian/Ubuntu sudo apt update && sudo apt install libpcap-dev Fedora/RHEL sudo dnf install libpcap-devel macOS (Homebrew) brew install libpcap

docs.title: Running from Source Code
docs.text:
To run the application without building an executable, use the standard Go command. Command-line arguments can be passed directly after the package path.

$ go run ./cmd/spoofdpi --https-chunk-size 1

docs.title: Building an Executable
docs.text:
To build the executable, ensure CGO is enabled and run the standard Go build command targeting the /cmd directory:

$ CGO_ENABLED=1 go build -ldflags="-w -s" ./cmd/...

docs.title: Code Quality
docs.text:
This project utilizes golangci-lint as the single entry point for both code quality checks (linting) and style enforcement (formatting). This ensures consistent code standards across the entire project.

- Format the code (using internal tools like goimports, gofmt)
$ golangci-lint fmt

- Run all quality checks
$ golangci-lint run

docs.title: Commit Messages
docs.text:
This project adheres to the Conventional Commits specification to ensure a clear and standardized project history. Please follow the format below.

type(scope): description

[optional body]

[optional footer(s)]

Allowed valus for <type>

  • feat: A new feature
  • fix: A bug fix
  • docs: Documentation only changes
  • style: Changes that do not affect the meaning of the code (white-space, formatting, missing semi-colons, etc)
  • refactor: A code change that neither fixes a bug nor adds a feature
  • perf: A code change that improves performance
  • test: Adding missing tests or correcting existing tests
  • chore: Other changes that don't modify src or test files
  • ci: Changes to our CI configuration files and scripts
  • revert: Reverts a previous commit

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text: This project utilizes the Material for MkDocs theme as a static site generator for project documentation.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
Install the necessary dependencies. We explicitly install the Material theme which should include MkDocs as a dependency.

$ pip install mkdocs-material

docs.title: Local Development
docs.text:
All documentation source files are located in the docs directory, and the configuration file mkdocs.yml is located in the project root.

To run the documentation site locally, execute the command below from the project root:

$ mkdocs serve

This command will start a development server (usually accessible at http://127.0.0.1:8000), which automatically reloads upon source file changes.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text: This document outlines how to run tests and the conventions for writing new tests in spoofdpi.

docs.title: Running Tests
docs.text:
To run tests that do not require network access, use the standard go test command from the root directory:

$ go test ./...

To run all tests, including tests that require network access, pass the network build tag:

$ go test -tags network ./...

To run all tests with verbose output (showing all test names):

$ go test -v -tags network ./...

To run a specific test function (e.g., TestCreateCommand_Flags):

$ go test -v -run TestCreateCommand_Flags ./internal/config/

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text: spoofdpi uses the standard testing package enhanced by testify for assertions and requirements.

docs.title: 1. Framework
docs.text:
• Use testify/assert for general assertions where a failure should record an error but continue the test.
  • Use testify/require for checks that must pass for the rest of the test to proceed (e.g., checking for errors after a function call, ensuring setup was successful).
import (
    "testing"
    "github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
    "github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

func TestExample(t *testing.T) {
    result, err := SomeFunction()

    // Stop immediately if there's an error
    require.NoError(t, err)

    // Assert the result, but continue even if it fails
    assert.Equal(t, "expected", result)
}

docs.title: 2. Table-Driven Tests
docs.text:
For testing multiple scenarios of the same logic, table-driven tests are strongly preferred. This keeps the test code clean and makes it easy to add new cases.

func TestCalculation(t *testing.T) {
    tcs := []struct {
        name     string
        input    int
        expected int
    }{
        {
            name:     "positive number",
            input:    5,
            expected: 10,
        },
        {
            name:     "zero",
            input:    0,
            expected: 0,
        },
    }

    for _, tc := range tcs {
        t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
            result := calculate(tc.input)
            assert.Equal(t, tc.expected, result)
        })
    }
}

docs.title: 3. Naming
docs.text:
• Test functions should start with Test followed by the name of the function or feature being tested (e.g., TestCreateCommand).
  • Use clear and descriptive names for table-driven test cases (e.g., name: "default values (no flags)").

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
spoofdpi requires the libpcap library on all operating systems except Linux.

- macOS
$ brew install libpcap 

- FreeBSD
$ pkg install libpcap

- Linux
$ echo "libpcap is not required on Linux"

- ...

docs.title: Install Using Script
docs.text:
You can install spoofdpi using the provided script. The binary will be installed to /usr/local/bin. 

$ curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xvzc/spoofdpi/main/install.sh | bash

docs.title: Install With Package Manager
docs.text:
You can also install spoofdpi using package managers of your choice, but note that the version may not be the latest, depending on the Packaging Status.

- macOS
$ brew install spoofdpi

- Arch Linux
$ yay -S spoofdpi

- Fedora
$ sudo dnf install spoofdpi

- FreeBSD
$ pkg install spoofdpi

- ...

docs.title: Manual Build
docs.text:
To build spoofdpi manually, ensure that you have Go 1.26 or higher and the libpcap library installed.

Note

libpcap is no longer required on Linux, so CGO does not need to be enabled.

docs.title: Git
docs.text:
If you are building manually from the latest commit, we recommend including the commit hash for better issue tracking.

#!/usr/bin/env sh

BUILD_INFO="git"
SRC="spoofdpi"
DIST="dist"

mkdir -p ./$DIST

git clone https://github.com/xvzc/spoofdpi.git

BUILD_LDFLAGS="-s -w"
BUILD_LDFLAGS="$BUILD_LDFLAGS -X 'main.commit=$(git -C ./$SRC rev-parse --short HEAD)'"
BUILD_LDFLAGS="$BUILD_LDFLAGS -X 'main.build=$BUILD_INFO'"

# You can disable CGO on Linux by setting `CGO_ENABLED=0`
CGO_ENABLED=1 go build -C ./$SRC \
  -ldflags "$BUILD_LDFLAGS" \
  -o ../$DIST/spoofdpi ./cmd/spoofdpi

docs.title: GitHub Release
docs.text:
You can also build directly from the release source code. This is particularly useful for platforms where native GitHub Actions runners are unavailable (e.g., FreeBSD), requiring manual packaging.

We recommend injecting version and build information during the build process to help maintainers track issues effectively.

Every release includes a custom source archive (e.g., spoofdpi-1.1.3.tar.gz) which contains a COMMIT file. You can use this file to embed the commit hash into the binary. 

#!/usr/bin/env bash

VERSION="#REPLACE_THIS_WITH_VERSION#"
BUILD_INFO="freebsd"
ASSET="spoofdpi-$VERSION.tar.gz"
SRC="spoofdpi-$VERSION"
DIST="dist"

curl -fsSL \
  https://github.com/xvzc/spoofdpi/releases/download/v$VERSION/$ASSET \
  -o ./$ASSET

tar -xvzf ./spoofdpi-$VERSION.tar.gz

BUILD_LDFLAGS="-s -w"
BUILD_LDFLAGS="$BUILD_LDFLAGS -X 'main.version=$VERSION'"
BUILD_LDFLAGS="$BUILD_LDFLAGS -X 'main.commit=$(cat ./$SRC/COMMIT)'"
BUILD_LDFLAGS="$BUILD_LDFLAGS -X 'main.build=$BUILD_INFO'"

# You can disable CGO on Linux by setting `CGO_ENABLED=0`
CGO_ENABLED=1 go build -C ./$SRC \
  -ldflags "$BUILD_LDFLAGS" \
  -o ../$DIST/spoofdpi ./cmd/spoofdpi

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: spoofdpi is a lightweight, flexible tool designed to circumvent Deep Packet Inspection (DPI) through advanced packet manipulation. It is written in Go, supports cross-platform execution, and operates with minimal overhead.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• High Performance: Low latency achieved through the Go runtime and cache
  • Built-in DNS Resolver: Use built-in DNS resolvers without a need to change system settings
  • Flexible Policies: Robust policy rule support based on domains (allow/ignore)
  • Easy Configuration: Simple setup via a TOML file
  • Cross-Platform: Runs on macOS, Linux and FreeBSD

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
spoofdpi provides a number of options to customize its behavior, and these options have default values. If it works as expected without customizing the option values, you can just run it as shown below. 

$ spoofdpi

If you can't get it working as expected, check User Guide for more information on customization.

docs.title: App Configuration
docs.text: Application-level settings including mode, logging, and system integration.

docs.title: app-mode
docs.text: type: string

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Specifies the proxy mode. (default: "http")

docs.title: Allowed Values
docs.text:
• http: HTTP proxy mode
  • socks5: SOCKS5 proxy mode
  • tun: TUN interface mode (transparent proxy)

Warning

SOCKS5 and TUN modes are currently Experimental. You might encounter unexpected behaviors or bugs. Feedback and bug reports are highly appreciated!

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Command-Line Flag 

$ spoofdpi --app-mode socks5

TOML Config 

[app]
mode = "socks5"

docs.title: listen-addr
docs.text: type: <ip:port>

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Specifies the IP address and port to listen on. (default: 127.0.0.1:8080 for http, 127.0.0.1:1080 for socks5)

If you want to run spoofdpi remotely (e.g., on a physically separated machine), set the IP part to 0.0.0.0. Otherwise, it is recommended to leave this option as default for security.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Command-Line Flag 

$ spoofdpi --listen-addr "0.0.0.0:8080"

TOML Config 

[app]
listen-addr = "0.0.0.0:8080"

docs.title: log-level
docs.text: type: string

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Specifies the logging verbosity.

Available values are debug, trace, info, warn, error, and disabled. (default: "info")

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Command-Line Flag 

$ spoofdpi --log-level trace

TOML Config 

[app]
log-level = "trace"

docs.title: no-tui
docs.text: type: boolean

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Disables the TUI and runs in headless mode. When set, the ASCII art banner is also suppressed. (default: false)

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Command-Line Flag 

$ spoofdpi --no-tui

TOML Config 

[app]
no-tui = true

docs.title: auto-configure-network
docs.text: type: boolean

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Specifies whether to automatically set up the system-wide proxy configuration. (default: false)

Important

This option is currently only supported on macOS.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Command-Line Flag 

$ spoofdpi --auto-configure-network

TOML Config 

[app]
auto-configure-network = true

docs.title: config
docs.text: type: string

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Specifies the path to a custom TOML config file. (default: none)

If this option is set, spoofdpi will not search the default directories.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Command-Line Flag 

$ spoofdpi --config ~/spoofdpi.toml

TOML Config 

# This option is not available in TOML config

docs.title: clean
docs.text: type: boolean

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Specifies whether to ignore all configuration files and run with default settings. (default: false)

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Command-Line Flag 

$ spoofdpi --clean

TOML Config 

# This option is not available in TOML config

docs.title: freebsd-fib
docs.text: type: integer

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Specifies the FIB (Forwarding Information Base) ID for FreeBSD routing table. (default: 1)

Valid range is 1-15. This option is only applicable on FreeBSD systems when using TUN mode.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Command-Line Flag 

$ spoofdpi --freebsd-fib 3

TOML Config 

[app]
freebsd-fib = 3

docs.title: version
docs.text: type: boolean

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Prints the version string and exits. (default: false)

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Command-Line Flag 

$ spoofdpi --version

TOML Config 

# This option is not available in TOML config

docs.title: Connection Configuration
docs.text: Settings for network connection timeouts and packet configuration.

docs.title: dns-timeout
docs.text: type: uint16

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Specifies the timeout (in milliseconds) for DNS connections. (default: 5000, max: 65535)

A value of 0 means no timeout.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Command-Line Flag 

$ spoofdpi --dns-timeout 3000

TOML Config 

[connection]
dns-timeout = 3000

docs.title: tcp-timeout
docs.text: type: uint16

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Specifies the timeout (in milliseconds) for TCP connections. (default: 10000, max: 65535)

A value of 0 means no timeout.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Command-Line Flag 

$ spoofdpi --tcp-timeout 5000

TOML Config 

[connection]
tcp-timeout = 5000

docs.title: udp-idle-timeout
docs.text: type: uint16

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Specifies the idle timeout (in milliseconds) for UDP connections. (default: 25000, max: 65535)

The connection will be closed if there is no read/write activity for this duration. Each read or write operation resets the timeout.

A value of 0 means no timeout.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Command-Line Flag 

$ spoofdpi --udp-idle-timeout 30000

TOML Config 

[connection]
udp-idle-timeout = 30000

docs.title: default-fake-ttl
docs.text: type: uint8

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Specifies the default Time To Live (TTL) value for fake packets. (default: 8)

This value is used for fake packets sent during disorder strategies. A lower value ensures fake packets expire before reaching the destination, while the real packets arrive successfully.

Note

The fake TTL should be less than the number of hops to the destination.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Command-Line Flag 

$ spoofdpi --default-fake-ttl 10

TOML Config 

[connection]
default-fake-ttl = 10

docs.title: DNS Configuration
docs.text: Settings controlling how domain names are resolved.

docs.title: mode
docs.text: type: string

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Specifies the default resolution mode for domains that do not match any specific rule. (default: "udp")

docs.title: Allowed Values
docs.text:
• udp: Standard DNS over UDP.
  • https: DNS over HTTPS (DoH).
  • system: Use the system's default resolver.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Command-Line Flag 

$ spoofdpi --dns-mode "https"

TOML Config 

[dns]
mode = "https"

docs.title: addr
docs.text: type: <ip:port>

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Upstream DNS server address for standard UDP queries. (default: 8.8.8.8:53)

This is used when dns-mode is set to udp.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Command-Line Flag 

$ spoofdpi --dns-addr "1.1.1.1:53"

TOML Config 

[dns]
addr = "1.1.1.1:53"

docs.title: https-url
docs.text: type: string

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Endpoint URL for DNS over HTTPS (DoH) queries. (default: "https://dns.google/dns-query")

This is used when dns-mode is set to https.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Command-Line Flag 

$ spoofdpi --dns-https-url "https://1.1.1.1/dns-query"

TOML Config 

[dns]
https-url = "https://1.1.1.1/dns-query"

docs.title: qtype
docs.text: type: string

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Filters DNS queries by record type (A for IPv4, AAAA for IPv6). (default: "ipv4")

Available values are "ipv4", "ipv6", and "all".

If your Internet Service Provider (ISP) doesn't support IPv6, it is recommended to set this option to "ipv4" for stability.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Command-Line Flag 

$ spoofdpi --dns-qtype "all"

TOML Config 

[dns]
qtype = "all"

docs.title: cache
docs.text: type: boolean

docs.title: Description
docs.text: If set, DNS records will be cached to improve performance and reduce latency. (default: false)

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Command-Line Flag 

$ spoofdpi --dns-cache

TOML Config 

[dns]
cache = true

docs.title: Configuration Examples
docs.text: This page provides various configuration examples to help you set up spoofdpi for different scenarios.

docs.title: Basic Setup
docs.text:
A minimal configuration to get started with DNS over HTTPS (DoH) and basic DPI bypass.

[dns]
mode = "https"
https-url = "https://dns.google/dns-query"

docs.title: Aggressive Bypass
docs.text:
If the default settings are not enough, you can try more aggressive settings. This configuration uses multiple fake packets and disorders the Client Hello.

[https]
fake-count = 5
fake-packet = [0x16, 0x03, 0x01] # Simple fake Client Hello prefix
disorder = true
split-mode = "chunk"
chunk-size = 1

docs.title: Rule-Based Routing
docs.text:
Route traffic differently based on the domain or IP address.

# Block ads
[[rules]]
name = "block ads"
match = { domains = ["ads.example.com"] }
block = true

# Bypass DPI for specific blocked site
[[rules]]
name = "unblock site"
match = { domains = ["blocked-site.com"] }
https = { fake-count = 2, disorder = true }

# Use local network directly (no processing)
[[rules]]
name = "local bypass"
match = { cidrs = ["192.168.0.0/16"] }
https = { skip = true }

docs.title: HTTPS Configuration
docs.text: Settings for manipulating HTTPS/TLS packets to bypass DPI.

docs.title: split-mode
docs.text: type: string

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Specifies the default packet fragmentation strategy to use for the Client Hello packet. (default: "sni")

docs.title: Allowed Values
docs.text:
• sni: Splits the packet right after the SNI extension.
  • random: Splits the packet at a random position.
  • chunk: Splits the packet into fixed-size chunks (controlled by https-chunk-size).
  • first-byte: Splits only the first byte of the packet.
  • custom: Uses custom segment plans (TOML only).
  • none: Disables fragmentation.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Command-Line Flag 

$ spoofdpi --https-split-mode sni

TOML Config 

[https]
split-mode = "sni"

docs.title: chunk-size
docs.text: type: uint8

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Specifies the chunk size in bytes for packet fragmentation. (default: 35, max: 255)

This value is only applied when https-split-mode is set to chunk. Try lower values if the default fails to bypass the DPI.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Command-Line Flag 

$ spoofdpi --https-chunk-size 1

TOML Config 

[https]
chunk-size = 1

docs.title: disorder
docs.text: type: boolean

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Specifies whether to disorder fragmented Client Hello packets. (default: false)

When enabled, this option varies the TTL of fragmented Client Hello packets, potentially causing them to arrive out of order. This complicates the packet reassembly process for DPI systems.

Note

If split mode is none, disordering does not occur.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Command-Line Flag 

$ spoofdpi --https-disorder

TOML Config 

[https]
disorder = true

docs.title: fake-count
docs.text: type: uint8

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Specifies the number of fake packets to be sent before the actual Client Hello. (default: 0)

Sending fake packets can trick DPI systems into inspecting invalid traffic, allowing the real Client Hello to pass through. If https-chunk-size is greater than 0, each fake packet will also be fragmented.

Note

spoofdpi must be run with root privileges to use this option effectively on some systems or configurations requiring raw socket access (though usually not required for standard usage, verify if this note from old docs is still accurate - kept for safety).

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Command-Line Flag 

$ spoofdpi --https-fake-count 7

TOML Config 

[https]
fake-count = 7

docs.title: fake-packet
docs.text: type: byte array

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Customizes the content of the fake packets used by https-fake-count. (default: built-in fake packet)

The value should be a sequence of bytes representing a valid (or semi-valid) TLS Client Hello or other protocol data.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Command-Line Flag Provide a comma-separated string of hexadecimal bytes (e.g., 0x16, 0x03, 0x01, ...).

$ spoofdpi --https-fake-packet "0x16, 0x03, 0x01, 0x00, 0xa1, ..."

TOML Config Provide an array of integers (bytes).

[https]
fake-packet = [0x16, 0x03, 0x01, 0x00]

docs.title: skip
docs.text: type: boolean

docs.title: Description
docs.text: If set to true, HTTPS traffic will be processed without any DPI bypass techniques (fragmentation, disordering, etc.). It effectively treats the connection as a standard HTTPS proxy connection.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Command-Line Flag 

$ spoofdpi --https-skip

TOML Config 

[https]
skip = true

docs.title: custom-segments
docs.text: type: array of segment plans

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Defines custom segmentation plans for fine-grained control over how the Client Hello packet is split. This option is only used when split-mode is set to "custom".

Each segment plan specifies where to split the packet relative to a reference point (from) with an offset (at).

Note

This option is only available via the TOML config file.

Important

When using custom split-mode, the global disorder option is ignored. Use the lazy field in each segment plan to control packet ordering instead.

docs.title: Segment Plan Fields
docs.text: Field Type Required Description from String Yes Reference point: "head" (start of packet) or "sni" (start of SNI extension). at Int Yes Byte offset from the reference point. Negative values count backwards. lazy Boolean No If true, delays sending this segment (equivalent to disorder). (default: false) noise Int No Adds random noise (in bytes) to the split position. (default: 0)

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
TOML Config

[https]
split-mode = "custom"
custom-segments = [
    { from = "head", at = 2 },                    # Split 2 bytes from start
    { from = "sni", at = 0 },                     # Split at SNI start
    { from = "sni", at = -5, lazy = true },       # Split 5 bytes before SNI, delayed
    { from = "head", at = 100, noise = 10 },      # Split at ~100 bytes with ±10 noise
]

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
There are two methods to configure spoofdpi, and both can be used together.

  • TOML Config File
  • Command-Line Flags

docs.title: Configuration Priority
docs.text:
spoofdpi applies settings in the following order:

  1. Values defined in the TOML config file
  2. Values passed via command-line (CLI) flags

Command-line flags will always override values set in the TOML config file. For example, if config.toml contains listen-addr = "127.0.0.1:8080", but the user runs $ spoofdpi --listen-addr :9090, the :9090 port will be used.

docs.title: Config File Path
docs.text:
If a specific path is not provided via a --config flag, spoofdpi will search for spoofdpi.toml in the following locations in order, applying only the first file found:

  • $SPOOFDPI_CONFIG environment variable
  • /etc/spoofdpi.toml
  • $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/spoofdpi/spoofdpi.toml
  • $HOME/.config/spoofdpi/spoofdpi.toml

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
The configuration is organized into six main categories. Click on each category to view detailed options.

Category Description App Application-level options (mode, address, logging, etc.). Connection Connection timeout and packet TTL settings. DNS DNS resolution options. HTTPS HTTPS/TLS packet manipulation options. UDP UDP packet manipulation options. Rules Rule-based routing and automatic bypass policies.

docs.title: Example
docs.text: The following two methods will achieve the exact same configuration.

docs.title: Method 1: Using Command-Line Flags
docs.text:
All settings are passed directly via flags.

$ spoofdpi --app-mode socks5 --dns-mode https --https-disorder

docs.title: Method 2: Using a TOML Config File
docs.text:
Place the settings in your spoofdpi.toml file:

[app]
mode = "socks5"

[dns]
mode = "https"

[https]
disorder = true

Then, run spoofdpi without those flags (it will automatically load the file if placed in a standard path):

$ spoofdpi

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
By defining rules, you can granularly control how spoofdpi handles connections to specific domains or IP addresses. You can define per-domain bypass strategies, DNS settings, or simply block connections.

Note

Rules are only available via the TOML config file and cannot be set via command-line flags.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text: The top-level [[rules]] array contains one table per rule. Each rule consists of matching criteria (match) and per-section overrides (dns, https, udp, connection).

docs.title: Rule Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description name String A descriptive name for the rule. priority Int Order of precedence. Higher numbers take priority. block Bool If true, completely blocks connections matching this rule.

docs.title: Match Criteria (match)
docs.text:
You can specify a domains list or a cidrs list.

Field Type Description domains Array List of domain patterns. Supports wildcards (*, **). cidrs Array List of IP ranges in CIDR notation (e.g., ["10.0.0.0/8"]).

docs.title: File-based match lists
docs.text:
Both domains and cidrs accept items with a file: prefix. The path after the prefix is read line by line, and each non-empty, non-comment line is treated as an additional item.

[[rules]]
name = "streaming"
match = { domains = ["file:assets/streaming-domains.txt", "*.youtube.com"] }
https = { fake-count = 5 }

Path resolution

Prefix / form Resolved against Relative path Directory of the config file Absolute path (/…) Used as-is ~/… User home directory $VAR/… Environment variable

File format rules

  • Lines beginning with # are treated as comments and ignored.
  • Blank lines are ignored.
  • If the file does not exist, a warning is emitted at startup and the entry is skipped (the server still starts).
  • Any other I/O error (e.g. permission denied) is fatal.
# assets/streaming-domains.txt
*.netflix.com
*.nflxvideo.net
# add more below

docs.title: DNS Override (dns)
docs.text:
Customize how domain names are resolved for matched traffic. The available fields mirror the global DNS Configuration.

Field Type Description mode String Resolver to use: "udp", "https" (DoH), or "system". addr String Custom upstream server (e.g., 8.8.8.8:53). https-url String Custom DoH URL (e.g., https://dns.google/dns-query). qtype String Query type: "ipv4", "ipv6", or "all". cache Bool If true, enables caching for this rule.

docs.title: HTTPS Override (https)
docs.text:
Customize how HTTPS connections are established. The available fields mirror the global HTTPS Configuration.

Field Type Description disorder Bool Send Client Hello packets out of order. fake-count Int Number of fake packets to send. fake-packet Array List of bytes for the fake packet (e.g., [0x16]). split-mode String Split strategy: "chunk", "sni", "random", etc. chunk-size Int Size of chunks when split-mode is "chunk". skip Bool If true, bypasses DPI modifications (standard TLS).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
# Example A: Allow YouTube with specific DPI bypass settings
[[rules]]
name = "allow youtube"
priority = 50
match = { domains = ["*.youtube.com"] }
https = { disorder = true, fake-count = 7 }

# Example B: Bypass DPI for local network traffic (Standard Connection)
[[rules]]
name = "skip local"
priority = 51
match = { cidrs = ["192.168.0.0/24"] }
https = { skip = true }

# Example C: Block a specific domain
[[rules]]
name = "block ads"
priority = 100
match = { domains = ["ads.example.com"] }
block = true

docs.title: Deprecated: [[policy.overrides]]
docs.text:
Earlier versions used [[policy.overrides]] instead of [[rules]]. The old key is still accepted for backward compatibility but emits a deprecation warning at startup. Migrate to the top-level [[rules]] form — it removes the [policy] indirection that no longer carries any other configuration.

# Deprecated form — still works, prints a warning
[[policy.overrides]]
name = "allow youtube"
match = { domains = ["*.youtube.com"] }
https = { fake-count = 7 }

docs.title: UDP Configuration
docs.text: Settings for UDP packet manipulation and bypass techniques.

docs.title: skip
docs.text: type: boolean

docs.title: Description
docs.text: If set to true, UDP traffic will be processed without any DPI bypass techniques (fake packets, etc.). It effectively treats the connection as a standard UDP proxy connection. (default: false)

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Command-Line Flag 

$ spoofdpi --udp-skip

TOML Config 

[udp]
skip = true

docs.title: fake-count
docs.text: type: int

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Specifies the number of fake packets to be sent before actual UDP packets. (default: 0)

Sending fake packets can trick DPI systems into inspecting invalid traffic, allowing real packets to pass through.

Note

This feature requires root privileges and packet capture capabilities.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Command-Line Flag 

$ spoofdpi --udp-fake-count 5

TOML Config 

[udp]
fake-count = 5

docs.title: fake-packet
docs.text: type: byte array

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Customizes the content of the fake packets used by udp-fake-count. (default: 64 bytes of zeros)

The value should be a sequence of bytes representing the fake packet data.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Command-Line Flag Provide a comma-separated string of hexadecimal bytes (e.g., 0x00, 0x01, 0x02, ...).

$ spoofdpi --udp-fake-packet "0x00, 0x01, 0x02, 0x03, 0x04"

TOML Config Provide an array of integers (bytes).

[udp]
fake-packet = [0x00, 0x01, 0x02, 0x03, 0x04]

docs.title: South Korea
docs.text:
# TOML config
https-chunk-size = 1
https-fake-count = 10
policy = [
    "i:*.pornhub.com",
    "i:*.womenonweb.org",
]
